title: Launch AWS DevOps Agent to review findings and test results from AWS Resilience Hub
text: The next generation of AWS Resilience Hub now integrates with AWS DevOps agent allowing you to review failure mode assessment findings and implement mitigations to resolve findings and review resilience test results. AWS Resilience Hub is a central location in the AWS Management Console that helps platform engineering and site reliability teams assess and strengthen the resilience of their workloads running on AWS. It provides automated dependency discovery, generative AI-powered failure mode analysis, modular resilience policies, resilience testing, and organization-wide resilience posture reporting. Resilience test investigations: When you run a resilience test, Resilience Hub now launches an AWS DevOps Agent investigation that observes the test and returns a structured analysis. You can uncover symptoms, root cause, and impact along with observed recovery actions, like ARC Region switch. Interactive agent analysis from failure mode assessment findings: You can now start AWS DevOps Agent on demand task directly from a failure mode assessment finding in the Resilience Hub console, with the finding's context already in place. This allows for asking questions and investigating findings to create a mitigation plan. To get started, visit the AWS Resilience Hub console , select a service and configure DevOps agent in the service configuration. Then launch the DevOps agent directly from a failure mode assessment finding or a resilience test. To learn more, see the product page or visit the documentation . AWS Resilience Hub is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Paris), Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Seoul), and South America (São Paulo).

title: AWS End User Messaging now offers managed OTP verification end-to-end
text: Today, AWS End User Messaging announces end-to-end managed one-time passcode (OTP) verification in Notify. You get a working OTP solution in under five minutes, including AWS phone numbers and code verification, without setting up a phone number, registering with carriers, or managing how messages are delivered. Before, you generated the passcode yourself and passed it to Notify to send, and you built and maintained the logic to create, store, and expire codes. Now Notify generates the code, delivers it, and verifies the code the recipient enters, so you ship a complete verification flow and skip that work entirely. You can deliver codes over text, voice, and now WhatsApp. You set the rules once in a notify code configuration: the code type, length, how long it stays valid, and how many attempts a recipient gets, along with your templates for each channel. From then on, one call sends a code to a recipient on the channel you choose, and another checks the code they enter. Notify is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS End User Messaging is available. To learn more and get started, see the AWS End User Messaging User Guide.

title: AWS End User Messaging now supports Brand Profiles
text: Today, AWS End User Messaging announces Brand Profiles, which let you store your brand and company information once and reuse it across your messaging registrations. To send messages on SMS, RCS, and WhatsApp, you register your brand with carriers and messaging providers, and today you fill in the same company details, address, contact information, and use case by hand on every form, for each channel and country. That repeated entry slows every new registration, and a typo or other error can get one rejected and delay when you can start sending. With Brand Profiles, you enter this information once and apply it to each new registration, so you register faster and keep your details consistent across channels and countries. You can use Brand Profiles whether you send for your own brand or manage several brands in a single AWS account. When you start a registration with a Brand Profile, the service fills in the matching fields from the information you saved and gives you a draft to review before you submit. By default, it matches standard fields such as company name, tax ID, address, and contact details. You can also turn on smart match, which uses AI to fill in fields even when their names differ. You can build a Brand Profile from scratch or start from your existing registrations. Brand Profiles is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS End User Messaging is available. To learn more and get started, see the AWS End User Messaging User Guide.

title: AWS HealthOmics expands container registry support for private workflows
text: You can now use container images from registries such as Seqera (Wave), NVIDIA NGC, and Google Artifact Registry with AWS HealthOmics expanded support for third-party container registries. You can use the containerized tools your workflows already rely on, without manually migrating images into Amazon ECR or editing your workflow definitions. AWS HealthOmics is a HIPAA-eligible service that helps healthcare and life sciences customers accelerate scientific breakthroughs at scale with fully managed bioinformatics workflows. With expanded container registry support, you can now instruct HealthOmics to copy container images, on your behalf, from newly supported registries into your Amazon ECR when running your private workflows. Previously, AWS HealthOmics could pull images only from registries supported through Amazon ECR pull-through cache (PTC). Your private workflows can now access Amazon ECR pull-through cache registries and the newly supported third party container registries, so you do not need to pull, re-push, or rewrite image URIs yourself. Expanded container registry support is now available in all AWS Regions where HealthOmics is available: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London), Israel (Tel Aviv), and Asia Pacific (Singapore, Seoul, Tokyo). To learn more, visit the third-party container image support documentation .

title: AWS IAM Identity Center extends multi-Region support to more AWS Regions
text: IAM Identity Center helps you connect your workforce identities to AWS once and streamline access management to AWS accounts and applications. You can now replicate IAM Identity Center to opt-in AWS Regions, and between Regions within the AWS GovCloud (US) and AWS China Regions. Previously, multi-Region support was available in the enabled-by-default commercial AWS Regions. This helps you improve the resilience of user access to AWS accounts and deploy AWS applications in the AWS Regions that best align with your business needs. When you enable multi-Region support, IAM Identity Center automatically replicates your identities, entitlements, and other information from the primary Region to additional Regions. If IAM Identity Center is affected by a disruption in the primary Region, users continue to have access to their AWS accounts using already provisioned entitlements in the additional Regions. AWS application administrators can use the standard application deployment workflow to deploy their application in an additional Region while you continue to administer IAM Identity Center in the primary Region. Multi-Region support is available for organization instances that use an external identity provider or the IAM Identity Center directory as the identity source, and requires a multi-Region customer managed KMS key (CMK). When you create a new instance, you can enable multi-Region support with a single click, which also creates the CMK. For existing instances, create a multi-Region CMK in AWS KMS, then configure it in IAM Identity Center. Standard AWS KMS charges apply for storing and using CMKs. IAM Identity Center is provided at no additional cost. For the full list of AWS Regions where multi-Region support is available, see AWS Capabilities by Region . To learn more about multi-Region support, see Using IAM Identity Center across multiple AWS Regions . To find out which AWS applications support deployment in additional Regions, visit AWS applications that you can use with IAM Identity Center .

title: AWS Lambda durable functions increases durable operation and checkpoint payload limits
text: Starting today, AWS Lambda durable functions increases the maximum number of durable operations per execution from 3,000 to 30,000, and the maximum checkpoint payload size from 256 KB to 1 MB. Higher operation limits let you safely do more work in a single execution including expanding iterative loops, polling for longer time periods, and building more complex rollback paths that run when a step fails. At 1 MB, checkpoint payloads match the maximum payload size of asynchronous Lambda invocations, and integration services such as Amazon SQS, and Amazon EventBridge, so a workflow can persist a full event from any of these sources in a single operation. AWS Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that execute for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing, automatic retries, and waits that suspend execution without incurring compute charges. Every durable operation counts toward the per-execution limit, including each step attempt, each poll of a wait-for-condition, and each branch of a parallel or map operation. With 30,000 operations, a single execution has more room to coordinate complex, multi-step workflows, iterate across thousands of items, or poll an external system for weeks, without exceeding checkpoint limits. An agentic application can reason over thousands of model and tool calls, and with 1 MB checkpoints it persists larger conversation histories, model responses, and outputs from tools directly in the checkpoint instead of writing to external storage. For state larger than 1 MB, the JavaScript and Python SDKs include a FileSystem serializer that writes the payload to an Amazon EFS or Amazon S3 Files mount and checkpoints a pointer instead. The new limits apply in all AWS Regions where AWS Lambda durable functions is available. To learn more about these service limits, see the AWS Lambda developer guide .

title: AWS Lambda announces Lambda Web Functions
text: AWS Lambda announces Lambda Web Functions, a new serverless compute primitive where your code handles HTTP requests directly. Your code listens on a port and handles requests as it would on any HTTP server. You use frameworks you already know, such as Express or Hono, with no adapters or custom configuration. This enables you to serve workloads such as AI inference endpoints, server-side rendered (SSR) web apps, streaming API endpoints, microservices, and webhooks. You pay for active CPU time and the memory your environment holds, not for idle CPU time your code spends waiting on databases or downstream services. With this launch, we are also renaming existing Lambda functions to Lambda Event Functions, a naming change only that requires no code changes or redeployments for your existing functions. Builders use Lambda to go from code to production quickly and without managing servers, across event-driven pipelines, request-response APIs, and data processing. As AI-driven development accelerates, they want to build locally and deploy with a familiar programming model and pay for workloads based on active CPU usage, while serving users with low latency. Lambda Web Functions delivers this. Today, Lambda Web Functions supports the Node.js runtime. A single warm execution environment can serve multiple concurrent requests, which reduces cold starts by orders of magnitude. You can stream results to clients incrementally with native HTTP streaming. You can create and configure Lambda Web Functions using the AWS Lambda API, Agent Toolkit for AWS , AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, AWS CloudFormation, AWS SAM, AWS CDK, or the AWS SDKs. With multi-Region routing, you can deploy once and serve each request from the Region closest to the end user. Web Functions support Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) connectivity, allowing your function to access resources that exist within a VPC. Lambda Web Functions is available today in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). For the current list, see the AWS Capabilities by Region page. To learn more, see the Lambda Web Functions developer guide . For pricing details, see AWS Lambda Pricing . To see Lambda Web Functions in action, see the AWS News Blog announcement .

title: AWS Network Firewall adds wildcard support for container attribute filters
text: AWS Network Firewall now supports wildcard matching in container attribute-based inspection filters for Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). This enhancement allows you to define attribute filters using wildcard patterns to match multiple container workloads in a single rule, eliminating the need to create individual container associations for each variant. With wildcard support, you can use patterns like app=payments-* to automatically cover all variants of an application, such as payments-api, payments-worker, and payments-cron. This simplifies firewall rule management for dynamic container environments where new application variants are frequently deployed, reducing operational overhead and ensuring consistent security coverage across your containerized workloads. Wildcard support for container attribute filters is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Network Firewall container attribute-based inspection is supported. For a full list of supported Regions, see the AWS Region Table . To get started, visit AWS Network Firewall product page and service documentation .

title: AWS Advanced Ruby Driver Wrapper is generally available
text: The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Advanced Ruby Driver Wrapper is now generally available for use with Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and MySQL-compatible databases. This advanced database driver reduces RDS Blue/Green switchover, Aurora Global database switchover and database failover times, improving application availability. Additionally, it supports multiple authentication mechanisms for your database, including AWS Secrets Manager authentication, and token-based authentication with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). The AWS Advanced Ruby Driver Wrapper builds on top of the community pg (PostgreSQL), and the mysql2 (MySQL) drivers to provide enhanced functionality beyond standard database connectivity. The wrapper is natively integrated with Aurora and RDS databases, enabling it to monitor database cluster status and quickly connect to newly promoted writers during unexpected failures that trigger database failovers. Furthermore, the wrapper seamlessly integrates with the ActiveRecord through provided aws_postgresql and aws_mysql2 adapters, so you can enable it without changing your application code. The driver is available as an open-source project under the Apache 2.0 license. Refer to the instructions on the GitHub repository to get started.

title: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring is now included in the AWS Security Hub Threat Analytics plan
text: Today, AWS announces that Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring is now included in the AWS Security Hub Threat Analytics plan. Runtime Monitoring inspects operating system, network, and file activity to surface threats such as container escapes, privilege escalation, and cryptomining on Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon EKS clusters, and Amazon ECS tasks on AWS Fargate. Security Hub now bills this coverage through streamlined pricing. If you have Security Hub enabled in an account and region, you no longer receive separate Amazon GuardDuty charges for Runtime Monitoring for that account and region. That usage now appears on your bill under AWS Security Hub, where Security Hub meters it as a single usage type that spans Amazon EC2, Amazon EKS, and Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate rather than as separate charges for each resource type. Your detection coverage, your finding types, and your GuardDuty security agents all remain the same, and you do not need to reconfigure anything. Please note that the free trial for the Threat Analytics plan remains separate from the free trial for the Security Hub Essentials plan, and that this change does not add a new free trial for Runtime Monitoring. To see how the change affects your bill, you can use AWS Cost Explorer or the Security Hub usage page. For a list of AWS Regions where Security Hub is available, see the AWS Region table . For pricing details, see the AWS Security Hub pricing page . To get started, visit the AWS Security Hub product page or console .

title: AWS Transform announces Azure-to-AWS cloud-native code conversion
text: Today, AWS announced the general availability of application code conversion from Azure SDK to AWS SDK in AWS Transform, giving you an accelerated path to migrate Microsoft Azure cloud-native .NET applications to AWS. The AWS Transform .NET modernization agent identifies Azure service code and converts it to equivalent AWS service code. For example, an Azure Functions serverless function that uses Azure Cosmos DB can be converted to an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon DynamoDB. AWS Transform discovers the Azure SDK in your submitted source code and presents the conversion options in the assessment report and modernization plan. You can accept the options provided or adjust them based on your preferences before running the modernization. AWS Transform then converts the identified Azure service code to the equivalent AWS SDK calls, and validates that the changes are incorporated into the transformed code. The feature supports conversion of Azure Functions to AWS Lambda functions, Azure Blob Storage to Amazon S3, and Azure Queue Storage to Amazon SQS, with Azure Cosmos DB to Amazon DynamoDB conversion available in preview. AWS Transform is available in eight AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney), Canada (Central), and Europe (Frankfurt, London). To learn more, see Convert cloud-native code to AWS in the AWS Transform User Guide.

title: AWS Transform now builds new networks and modernizes security groups
text: AWS Transform for migrations now gives you three ways to bring your network to AWS. In addition to migrating and modernizing your existing network, you can build a new network from scratch or convert your on-premises access rules into optimized security groups and deploy them into existing VPCs. Whichever path you choose, you arrive on AWS with a secure and scalable network foundation. On-premises networks accumulate years of definitions and access rules that you may not want to carry to AWS as-is. For a clean start, AWS Transform builds a new network aligned to AWS best practices. To bring your access rules with you, AWS Transform converts them into security groups and modernizes them as it goes, detecting stale rules and recommending optimizations, then deploys the groups into your existing VPCs without redeploying your network stack. These capabilities allow you migrate to any AWS commercial or GovCloud Region . To get started, see Migrate networks . To learn more, visit AWS Transform for migrations .

title: AWS Well-Architected Agent is now available in preview
text: AWS announces the preview of AWS Well-Architected Agent, an AI-powered service that is the next-gen evolution of AWS Trusted Advisor and the AWS Well-Architected Tool. The agent analyzes and optimizes AWS infrastructure across cost, security, performance, and reliability, delivering contextualized recommendations prioritized by business goals. It automatically correlates key metrics and application topology against Well-Architected best practices and analyzes Terraform, CDK templates and CloudFormation templates to deliver automation-ready fixes where applicable. With AWS Well-Architected Agent, teams can define their business goals and get recommendations prioritized by impact and effort at the resource, application, and architecture levels. For example, a team prioritizing reliability can receive recommendations to add multi-AZ failover to a critical database, complete with an SSM runbook that automates the configuration change and a cross-pillar analysis showing how this change affects cost and performance before you commit. Where applicable, recommendations are delivered with SSM runbooks, prescriptive CLI scripts, and guided console walkthroughs so teams can move quickly. The agent can also conduct automated reviews of your IaC templates that include Terraform, CloudFormation, or CDK templates, identifying gaps, and returning the IaC code changes needed to align with Well-Architected best practices. Access to the AWS Well-Architected Agent and its recommendations is available in US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), and US West (Oregon). You can onboard workloads from any AWS commercial Region. AWS Well-Architected Agent is delivered by AWS Support and available to AWS customers with an AWS Support plan. Learn more about AWS Well-Architected Agent in the User Guide . Get started here .

title: Amazon Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization now supports prompt shortening
text: Amazon Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization now supports prompt shortening, an optional setting that reduces the length of your prompt while maintaining or improving your evaluation scores. Advanced Prompt Optimization optimizes prompts for any model on Amazon Bedrock against your own evaluation criteria. Until now, optimization focused on quality alone. Optimized prompts were often longer than the original. Longer prompts raise input token costs and can increase time to first token, which matters at scale and in latency-sensitive applications. When you turn on prompt shortening for a prompt template in your input dataset, the optimizer reduces the prompt's length. The optimized prompt is returned only when it is shorter than your original prompt and scores at least as high on your evaluation. Otherwise your original prompt is returned, so the setting never leaves you with a longer or lower-scoring prompt. Results include a compression ratio and the original and optimized token counts, in the output file and on the console results page. For example, a compression ratio of 0.7 means the optimized prompt uses 30% fewer tokens. Prompt shortening works with any evaluation method, including steering criteria, LLM-as-a-judge rubrics, and custom Lambda evaluators. Prompt shortening is available in all AWS Regions where Advanced Prompt Optimization is available. To get started, enable prompt shortening for a prompt template in your input dataset and create an optimization job as usual. To learn more, see Shorten prompts in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide, the Amazon Bedrock pricing page , and the Amazon Bedrock product page .

title: Amazon Braket now in scope for FedRAMP Class C
text: Amazon Braket is now in scope for FedRAMP Class C in AWS US Regions where Braket is available. The Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) is a US government-wide program that delivers a standard approach to the security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring of cloud products and services. With FedRAMP Class C authorization, government customers and the organizations that serve them can use Amazon Braket to explore quantum computing within an authorized boundary. The AWS-operated components of Braket, including the API and SDK, job orchestration and management, compilation, and result storage in Amazon S3, are within the FedRAMP-certified boundary, while quantum workloads execute on third-party Quantum Hardware Providers (QHPs) outside that boundary. All data sent to QHPs meets AWS' privacy and security requirements including removal of all personally identifiable information, data encryption in transit and at rest, and adherence to AWS' standard data retention and deletion policies. To learn more about FedRAMP, visit AWS FedRAMP services and the FedRAMP Marketplace. To learn more about Amazon Braket, visit the Braket product page and Getting Started on Braket resources. Regional Availability: US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon)

title: Claude Haiku 5.5 is now available on AWS
text: AWS now offers Claude Haiku 5.5, the fastest and most efficient model in the Claude 5.5 family, built for subagents and high-volume, cost-sensitive work. According to Anthropic, it costs around 75% less than Claude Haiku 4.5 for most tasks. Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's most capable Haiku yet, a significant step up from Haiku 4.5 across coding, tool use, computer use, and agents. It's also the first Haiku with effort controls, so teams can tune cost against intelligence for each task. Haiku 5.5 fits work where speed and cost matter most: real-time experiences like voice agents, live support, and in-app assistants, and high-volume tasks like classification, summarization, and pulling key fields from documents. It's also a fast, cost-efficient subagent. A more capable model like Claude Opus 5.5 can plan the work and hand off well-defined coding, tool use, and browser automation tasks to Haiku, making it practical to run many agents in parallel. Customers have two ways to access Claude Haiku 5.5: Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Amazon Bedrock gives you Haiku's capabilities while keeping your data within AWS infrastructure with regional data residency and provides access through a unified service with AWS-managed features like Guardrails and Knowledge Bases. To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation and regional availability . Claude Platform on AWS gives you direct access to Anthropic's native platform experience and capabilities via the AWS Console. Build, test, and deploy with the same APIs, features, and console experience you'd get working with Anthropic directly, unified with AWS billing and authentication. To get started, see the Claude Platform on AWS documentation.

title: Amazon CloudFront now supports AWS Lambda Web Functions as an origin
text: Starting today, you can deliver web applications built on AWS Lambda Web Functions through CloudFront's global edge network. With CloudFront in front of a Lambda Web Function, you get TLS termination at the edge for lower latency and faster connections, caching for better performance, and custom domains with managed TLS certificates. No changes to application code are needed. CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) restricts your Lambda Web Function so it's reachable only through CloudFront, so unintended requests that bypass your security protections do not reach your origin. With OAC in place, CloudFront's edge network protects your Lambda Web Function from network-layer DDoS attacks, and you can attach AWS WAF for additional application-layer security. For applications that authenticate their own users, OAC ensures that original credentials reach the application unchanged, so existing sign-in flows keep working. CloudFront support for AWS Lambda Web Functions is available worldwide, except in the CloudFront China region. To get started, use the CloudFront Console, SDK, CLI, or CloudFormation to configure your Lambda Web Function as a CloudFront origin. For more information, refer to the CloudFront Developer Guide . There are no additional fees associated with this feature.

title: Amazon Cognito extends multi-Region replication to AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
text: Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication (MRR) now supports AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, extending the resilience benefits of MRR to more workloads. MRR lets you synchronize user and machine identity data, including credentials, user pool configurations, and federation setups, to a secondary user pool in a standby Region you designate, in near real-time. With user data in the standby Region, you can redirect traffic and keep authentication available if there is a disruption in your primary Region. Previously, MRR was available in 16 commercial Regions. You can now also use MRR to replicate between additional AWS Regions, helping you meet resilience, data residency, and compliance requirements in the Regions that best align with your business needs. MRR is available as an add-on for user pools in the Essentials or Plus feature tiers, and requires a multi-Region AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK). For the full list of AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available, see AWS Capabilities by Region . To get started, visit the developer guide for instructions and the pricing page for pricing details.

title: Amazon Connect Customer now lets you view metrics by customer lifetime value and repeat-caller status
text: Now you can view your metrics across customer segments: customer lifetime value (LTV) and repeat callers. See how any metric differs for repeat callers versus the rest of your contacts, or how results hold up among your highest-LTV customers; so you can spot the groups trending the wrong way before it shows up in the aggregate. Where a segment is underperforming, you can act. Route high-LTV customers to your most effective people, adjust the knowledge bases and self-service flows that repeat callers are falling back from, or refine agent guidance for segments where satisfaction is slipping. The segment tells you where to look; the metrics tell you what to fix.

title: Amazon Connect Customer now prefills step-by-step guides for after contact work
text: Amazon Connect Customer can now fill in the step-by-step guides that agents complete after a contact, using information extracted from customer conversations, such as booking identifiers, claim numbers, and conversation summaries. Managers can set which information populates each form field. Agents can review and submit rather than manually typing in each field, saving time and improving data accuracy during after contact work. Contact center agents spend time after each contact entering frequently used information into a step-by-step guide. For example, an insurance agent who finishes a claims call might record the customer’s policy number, a summary of the call, and a disposition code. Now, managers can define rules for which information to extract from the conversation and which fields to automatically fill in the guide. The agent can then check the information, make any necessary corrections, and submit the guide, shortening after contact work and reducing data entry errors. You can use step-by-step guides with information extraction in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). Contact summaries are also available in Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, see step-by-step guides in the Amazon Connect Customer administrator guide.

title: AWS Deadline Cloud now helps users find their accessible resources in the Deadline Cloud monitor
text: AWS Deadline Cloud now lets users who have access to specific queues, fleets, or jobs, rather than an entire farm, find the resources they can reach directly from the Deadline Cloud monitor. Deadline Cloud is a fully managed service that helps teams run compute-intensive workloads for visual effects, animation, product design, simulation, and gaming. Previously, a user with access to only one queue had to get the farm ID from an administrator before they could reach their work. With this launch, the Deadline Cloud monitor displays to users queues they have access to, the parent IDs needed to reach them, and their level of access, covering both direct and group-inherited permissions. Teams now can share a single monitor entry point (URL) across different permission levels without additional coordination. Resource discovery is available in all AWS Regions where Deadline Cloud is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Deadline Cloud user guide .

title: Amazon EC2 introduces shared tags for Amazon Machine Images
text: Amazon EC2 now supports AMI tag sharing, a new feature that lets AMI owners make selected tags visible to all AWS accounts an AMI is shared with. Whether an AMI is shared with an account, across an organization, or made public, a shared tag is automatically shared alongside the AMI, eliminating the need to build and maintain custom tag replication workflows. AMI owners simply add the 'ec2:SharedTag/' prefix to any tag key, and every account the AMI is shared with can immediately see it. This removes the operational burden of replicating tags into each account after sharing an AMI. Shared tags are read-only for recipient accounts, so only the owner can create, modify, or delete them. They count only against the owner's 50 tag per resource quota, allowing recipient accounts to continue adding their own private tags without any impact to their limits. This feature is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost. To learn more, please visit the documentation and read the blog .

title: Amazon EC2 C9g, C9gd, M9g, and M9gd instances are now available in additional regions
text: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) C9g and C9gd instances are available in the Asia Pacific (Malaysia, Seoul, Singapore) regions. Amazon EC2 M9g and M9gd instances are available in the Asia Pacific (Malaysia) and Europe (Spain) regions. These instances are powered by AWS Graviton5 processors, the fifth generation of custom-designed CPUs, which deliver the best price performance for a broad range of workloads running on Amazon EC2. C9g and C9gd instances and M9g and M9gd instances deliver up to 25% better compute performance than AWS Graviton4-based C8g, C8gd, M8g, and M8gd instances. They are up to 30% faster for databases, up to 35% faster for web applications, and up to 35% faster for machine learning. These instances are built on the sixth-generation AWS Nitro System and are the first to feature the Nitro Isolation Engine . The Isolation Engine uses formal verification to provide mathematical assurance that customer workloads are isolated from each other and from AWS operators, pioneering a new standard for mathematically proven cloud security. C9g instances are ideal for compute-intensive workloads such as high-performance computing (HPC), batch processing, gaming, video encoding, scientific modeling, distributed analytics, CPU-based machine learning (ML) inference, real-time analytics, and ad serving. M9g instances serve a broad range of general-purpose workloads, including application servers, microservices, gaming, caching, and containers. They also deliver the performance needed for agentic AI use cases like real-time reasoning, code generation, and multi-step orchestration. C9gd and M9gd instances add local NVMe-based SSD block-level storage for workloads that need high-speed, low-latency local storage for scratch space, temporary files, and caches. C9g, C9gd, M9g, and M9gd instances are available for purchase in these regions via Savings Plans, On-Demand, Spot Instances, Dedicated Instances, or Dedicated Hosts. Level up your compute with AWS Graviton and get started today with C9g and M9g .

title: Amazon EC2 T8i instances are now available in South America (São Paulo)
text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) T8i instances are now available in South America (São Paulo). These instances are powered by custom sixth generation Intel Xeon 6 processors, available exclusively on AWS, and built on the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards. T8i instances deliver up to 30% better price performance compared to previous generation T3 instances, and offer four sizes: nano, micro, small, and medium. These instances are designed for workloads requiring low to moderate CPU utilization, including data processing, login gateways, small databases, batch processing, event driven functions, CI/CD pipelines, microservices, and low traffic websites. T8i instances deliver up to 70% higher compute performance, 1.25x higher network bandwidth, and 2.4x higher EBS bandwidth compared to T3 instances. They use the same CPU credit system as T3 with Standard and Unlimited modes, so existing T3 customers can upgrade to T8i and immediately benefit from better price performance, enabling them to lower their TCO. For customers new to AWS or migrating from on-premises, T8i instances provide one of the most cost-effective entry points to run a variety of workloads. T8i.micro and T8i.small are available under the AWS Free Tier . T8i instances are available in US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon, N. California), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Paris), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad, Malaysia, Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo), Canada (Central) and South America (São Paulo) regions. T8i instances are available to purchase via On-Demand instances, and Spot instances with Savings Plan option coming soon. To learn more, visit the Amazon EC2 T8i instances page .

title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports advanced compute configuration
text: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) Auto Mode now lets you tune kubelet settings, Linux kernel sysctls, and hugepages directly in the NodeClass Kubernetes resource. You can now run workloads that require specific node tuning on EKS Auto Mode, which automates node provisioning, scaling, patching, and upgrades for you. With the new advancedCompute field in NodeClass, you can configure user namespaces for rootless container builds in CI/CD pipelines, tune eviction thresholds and container log rotation to protect nodes from disk and memory pressure, raise network and ARP cache limits for large clusters, and pre-allocate 2Mi or 1Gi hugepages for HPC, database, and latency-sensitive workloads. You apply these settings declaratively using the Kubernetes API. EKS Auto Mode validates them, applies them at node boot, and preserves them through scaling and upgrade events, so your workloads get the tuning they need while EKS Auto Mode continues to manage the underlying infrastructure, with no EC2 launch templates, custom AMIs, or privileged DaemonSets to maintain. Amazon EKS Auto Mode advanced compute configuration is available in all AWS Regions where EKS Auto Mode is available. To get started, see the Amazon EKS Auto Mode product page, and see Create a Node Class for Amazon EKS in the Amazon EKS documentation.

title: Serverless Storage on Amazon EMR Serverless now supports terabyte-scale shuffle
text: Amazon EMR Serverless now offers enhanced serverless storage capabilities with support for up to 1TB shuffle operations, raising the previous 200 GB per-job limit. Amazon EMR Serverless makes it simple for data engineers and data scientists to run open-source big data analytics frameworks without configuring, managing, and scaling clusters or servers. This enhancement enables enterprise customers to run production-scale Apache Spark workloads that require processing large volumes of shuffle data during complex operations such as joins, aggregations, and sorting. Enterprise data teams can now confidently migrate production workloads that routinely process terabyte-scale datasets without worrying about storage constraints. This enhancement is particularly valuable for workloads involving large table joins across multi-terabyte datasets, and complex aggregations on high-cardinality data that require extensive data shuffling. The addition of spill support ensures that jobs can seamlessly handle memory-intensive operations by offloading data to disk when necessary, improving job reliability and success rates for demanding analytical workloads. This feature is available with Amazon emr-7.14, emr-spark-8.1 and later, in 18 AWS Regions where Amazon EMR Serverless is available. See the Amazon EMR documentation for the full list of supported Regions and their applicable limits. To learn more about Amazon EMR Serverless and get started with terabyte-scale shuffle support, visit the Amazon EMR Serverless page .

title: Amazon GuardDuty RDS Protection now detects data exfiltration and destruction in Aurora and RDS databases
text: Amazon GuardDuty announces an expansion of RDS Protection that extends threat detection beyond login anomalies to identify data exfiltration and data destruction attacks targeting Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases. Available as RDS Protection for data activity, this new capability uses machine learning (ML)-based anomaly detection and integrated threat intelligence to continuously monitor database query patterns, helping you detect unusual data activity without requiring any agents, additional infrastructure, or database configuration changes. As attackers increasingly target databases to exfiltrate or destroy critical data after obtaining valid credentials through phishing, social engineering, or misconfiguration, their malicious database activity can appear indistinguishable from legitimate application behavior. RDS Protection for data activity establishes behavioral baselines for normal query patterns enabling GuardDuty to detect threats that traditional tools miss. You can enable GuardDuty RDS Protection for data activity as an add-on to RDS Protection for login activity. With a single click, they can enable it for their entire organization in the GuardDuty console, or programmatically via APIs, SDKs, CLI, or AWS CloudFormation. A 30-day free trial is available per account per Region. This feature is available today in all AWS commercial Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, where Amazon GuardDuty RDS Protection is offered with support for Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. For supported versions visit GuardDuty RDS Protection documentation . To learn more and start your free trial, visit the Amazon GuardDuty product page .

title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports optimistic locking for users and groups in its identity store
text: IAM Identity Center helps you configure the single sign-on experience of your workforce to AWS accounts and applications. You can now use optimistic locking for users and groups in the identity store, so that update and delete requests succeed only if the user or group hasn't changed since you last read it. This helps when multiple administrators or automated workflows modify the same user or group at nearly the same time, where previously one write could silently overwrite another. Each user and group now has a Revision value that changes every time the user's or group's attributes are modified, including through SCIM provisioning, Active Directory sync, or the IAM Identity Center console. Create, describe, update, and list operations return the current Revision, and you can pass it on a later UpdateUser, UpdateGroup, DeleteUser, or DeleteGroup request. The request succeeds only if the supplied Revision matches the current Revision. Otherwise, it returns a ConflictException, so your workflow can re-read the user or group and retry with the latest values. Providing a Revision is optional. Requests that omit it behave as before, so existing integrations continue to work without changes. Conditional requests are supported through the Identity Store API, not the SCIM endpoint. Group membership operations don't accept a Revision, and adding or removing members doesn't change the Revision of the user or the group. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. IAM Identity Center is provided at no additional cost. To learn more about IAM Identity Center, visit the product detail page. To get started, see UpdateUser in the Identity Store API Reference .

title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 4 additional AWS regions
text: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 4 additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Thailand), and Europe (Spain). With this launch, you can use Lambda MicroVMs in a total of 14 AWS Regions. Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume speeds, and state preservation for executing user or AI generated code. Developers can use Lambda MicroVMs to give each user or job their own isolated compute environment without managing virtualization infrastructure or choosing between isolation, speed, and state retention. MicroVMs enable secure, stateful, and responsive code execution for applications including AI coding assistants, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners. With today's launch, developers can run Lambda MicroVMs closer to their end-users in 4 additional Regions, helping meet latency and data residency requirements. To get started, create a MicroVM image from your Dockerfile, then launch MicroVMs from that image. Give each user or job their own MicroVM with a dedicated HTTPS URL that supports popular connectivity protocols such as HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSockets. You can use MicroVMs through the AWS Lambda console, AWS CloudFormation, AWS Cloud Development Kit, or with your preferred Agentic development tools using the Agent Toolkit for AWS . To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda MicroVMs developer guide . For information on pricing, see Lambda MicroVMs pricing . Visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page for the latest region availability.

title: Announcing the AWS Marketplace and Amazon Business unified storefront
text: Today, AWS Marketplace and Amazon Business announced the unified storefront. Organizations can now give their teams one curated catalog that puts software, data, and AI tools from AWS Marketplace alongside physical goods and supplies from Amazon Business. Many enterprises already buy from both, but they manage two catalogs with duplicated approval rules and separate reporting. The unified storefront can now give procurement teams one front door for both. Built on AWS Marketplace Storefront, the unified storefront lets administrators connect their organization's Amazon Business account and import Amazon Business products into their branded storefront. Administrators set governance rules once, and they apply across both catalogs. Buyers can browse AWS Marketplace listings and Amazon Business products in one place. Purchases of AWS Marketplace listings complete directly in the storefront and appear on the customer's AWS invoice. When a buyer selects an Amazon Business product, single sign-on takes them to an authenticated Amazon Business cart, so they don't need a second login. Each storefront connects only to the accounts its administrator sets up. The Amazon Business connector is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace operates to AWS Marketplace Storefront customers who have access to both the AWS Marketplace and Amazon Business APIs. To learn more, visit the AWS Marketplace Storefront product page and the AWS Marketplace Storefront User Guide .

title: SageMaker MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16
text: Amazon SageMaker AI MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16, bringing a redesigned tracing experience and faster experiment tracking to your generative AI and machine learning workflows. MLflow 3.16 improves debugging and analysis of generative AI applications and agents. The redesigned trace explorer is now the default, with adjustable row height, reorderable columns, custom columns from any trace tag or metadata field. This release also accelerates metric charts for experiments with large metric histories. New MLflow Apps are created on MLflow 3.16 by default. Existing MLflow Apps will be upgraded to MLflow 3.16 during an upcoming maintenance window, with no action required. MLflow 3.16 is available in all AWS Regions where MLflow Apps are available. To learn more, visit the SageMaker AI MLflow developer guide .

title: AWS HealthOmics now supports shared VPCs
text: AWS HealthOmics now supports sharing VPCs across accounts, enabling your workflows to access resources in Amazon Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) managed by other AWS accounts with AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM). AWS HealthOmics is a HIPAA-eligible service that helps healthcare and life sciences customers accelerate scientific breakthroughs at scale with fully managed bioinformatics workflows. With shared VPCs, customers can centralize networking administration by sharing subnets and security groups from a single VPC across multiple accounts in their organization, and HealthOmics then places each account's workflows directly into those shared subnets. With cross-account VPC sharing, multiple accounts run inside one centrally managed VPC, instead of duplicating endpoints across VPCs. Workflows in participating accounts can access data privately without separate VPC peering connections or duplicated VPC endpoints. Previously, customers with centralized networking had to create separate AWS PrivateLink VPC endpoints in each VPC and maintain individual route tables using VPC peering. Cross-account VPC sharing reduces infrastructure overhead and simplifies network management for organizations with centralized networking while allowing researchers and developers to run bioinformatics workflows in their own accounts. Shared VPCs is available in all Regions where AWS HealthOmics is available: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London), Israel (Tel Aviv), and Asia Pacific (Singapore, Seoul, Tokyo). To get started, see the AWS HealthOmics User Guide .

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports index-level encryption
text: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports index-level encryption, letting you encrypt each index at rest with its own AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. This helps you protect data with different ownership or sensitivity under separate keys on the same domain. For example, you can encrypt each tenant's data with its own key in a multi-tenant application. Index-level encryption builds on the existing encryption at rest capability in Amazon OpenSearch Service. To enable it, set the encryption mode to Native and specify a customer managed AWS KMS key when you create a new domain using the AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI. You can then register additional keys with the domain and use them to encrypt individual indexes. Index-level encryption is available for domains running OpenSearch version 3.3 or later in 14 AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Paris), and South America (São Paulo). There is no additional charge for the feature. Standard AWS KMS and OpenSearch Service charges apply. To get started, see Index-level encryption in the Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide.

title: AWS Partner Central launches Program Navigator, Case Study Generator, and streamlined specialization review
text: AWS Partner Central now features Program Navigator, a unified experience that lets partners discover, apply for, and track AWS Specialization program applications in one place. Partners can browse specialization designations, view requirements and benefits, and submit applications through a guided, step-by-step workflow. The new Case Study Generator in AWS Partner Central gives partners a redesigned creation experience with three starting paths: build a case study directly with AI assistance, import from an existing customer success story URL, or auto-populate from an opportunity. Case studies created for go-to-market purposes now follow a streamlined review path, a lightweight policy validation that lets partners publish directly to AWS domains without a specialization review. The deeper specialization-level review applies only to case studies associated with Program Navigator applications. Additionally, AWS has streamlined the specialization application review process through Program Navigator. Partners submitting applications can expect faster review times and more detailed, requirement-level feedback throughout the process. Partners applying for non-specialization programs continue to access those programs through the existing experience. Program Navigator and Case Study Generator are available to all AWS Partners in AWS Partner Central . To get started, navigate to Program Navigator and Case Studies under the Go to Market section in the left navigation panel.

title: Quick now supports smart approvals for agentic actions
text: Amazon Quick now supports smart approvals, a review layer that reduces unnecessary approval prompts while preserving human oversight of the actions that matter most. As agents take more actions on a user's behalf, such as sending email, updating records, and creating tickets, asking a person to approve every step leads to approval fatigue and weaker oversight over time. With smart approvals, a separate review model called the classifier evaluates each eligible action against the user's request. It approves routine actions automatically and refers consequential actions to the user for review. Your existing policies always come first. Smart approvals only reviews actions where the user's setting is "ask" each time. Denied actions stay denied, and smart approvals never grants new access. The classifier sends higher-impact actions to the user for review. These include sending content outside the organization, changing permissions, deleting content, making payments, and actions that go beyond what the user asked for. Each automatic approval covers only the exact action that was reviewed. If a review fails or times out, the action goes to the user. Smart approvals is on for all users by default. Administrators control who can use it with custom permissions, and users can turn it off for their conversations and scheduled runs in chat options. AWS CloudTrail records each action review made through smart approvals and each change to a user's smart approvals setting. Smart approvals is available in Amazon Quick in all AWS Regions where Amazon Quick agentic capabilities are supported. For more information, see the AWS Region table . To learn more about smart approvals, see smart approvals in the Amazon Quick User Guide. For more information about Amazon Quick, see the Amazon Quick product page .

title: Amazon Redshift now supports cross-Region queries for your data lake
text: Amazon Redshift now supports querying Amazon S3 data lake tables located in a different AWS Region. With enhanced VPC routing, data lake query traffic between Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift stays within your own VPC. Both capabilities are powered by the integrated data lake query engine that runs directly on the compute of RG provisioned and Serverless clusters. These features are aimed at enterprises with globally distributed data and at security-sensitive customers who need tight control over how their data travels. With cross-Region support, you can use Amazon Redshift to query S3 data in another Region directly, without first copying or replicating it. This makes it easier to run global analytics, consolidate reporting across Regions, and query data that must remain in a specific Region for residency requirements. Cross-Region queries incur standard data transfer charges. Because the query engine runs on your cluster's compute, data moving between Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift flows entirely over your VPC when you use enhanced VPC routing, never over public networks. Regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, and government benefit from this feature as it keeps data lake queries within the network boundaries their compliance requirements demand. Both capabilities work with the integrated data lake query engine, which is available in all regions where RG provisioned and Serverless clusters are available. To learn more, see Querying your data lake tables with enhanced VPC routing in the Amazon Redshift documentation .

title: ARC Region switch adds four new capabilities
text: Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) Region switch helps you orchestrate the failover of multi-Region applications to achieve a bounded recovery time during a Regional impairment. Today, Region switch adds four new capabilities: AWS Systems Manager Run Command execution block, payloads for custom action Lambda execution block, service quota parity checks, and wait for target group health feature for compute scaling actions. AWS Systems Manager Run Command execution block. During failover, you often need to run commands on managed instances and VMs. This execution block lets you invoke Run Command actions on managed instances during failover, with plan evaluation verifying that command documents target valid instances and that IAM permissions are correctly configured. Payloads for custom action Lambda execution block. ARC Region switch now lets you pass payloads to your custom action Lambda execution block, allowing reusability of your Lambda functions across recovery plans. Service quota checks. Service quota limits are a common failure mode during recovery. Region switch now verifies quota parity between your primary and standby Region, and automatically submits quota limit increases, reducing the risk of insufficient service quotas during recovery. Wait for target group health. Amazon ECS service scaling and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group execution blocks help you provision compute capacity during recovery, but provisioned capacity may not be ready to serve traffic. The optional wait for target group health feature verifies that your provisioned capacity is ready to serve traffic. To get started, see the documentation for AWS Systems Manager Run Command execution block , custom action Lambda execution block , Service quota checks and the Wait for target group health for Amazon ECS service scaling execution block and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group execution block .

title: Amazon Route 53 now supports registrations, transfers, and renewals for Premium Domains
text: Amazon Route 53 Domains now supports Premium Domain Names. Customers can now search for, register, transfer, renew, and restore registry premium names directly through Route 53. Most domain registries set aside a selection of "premium" domains - names that are short, memorable, or in high demand. Previously, Route 53 Domains did not support these premium names, which meant customers who wanted them had to register and manage them through other registrars, fragmenting their portfolios across multiple providers. With this launch, customers can now discover and acquire premium domains directly in Route 53 Domains, consolidate their existing premium domains from other registrars, and manage premium and standard domains together through a single, unified experience. Finding and registering a premium domain works just like it does for standard domains. Premium domains appear automatically in domain search and availability results, with pricing shown upfront, so customers know the cost before they commit. To learn more about Amazon Route 53 Domains and start registering premium domains, visit the Amazon Route 53 Domains page . For a complete list of supported top-level domains, see the Route 53 TLD list .

title: Amazon S3 Vectors metadata pre-filtering is now available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
text: Amazon S3 Vectors metadata pre-filtering is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West) Regions. Pre-filtering evaluates metadata filters before running similarity search, returning up to 5x more of the matching vectors when your filter is selective. S3 Vectors also adds a prefix match operator ($startsWith) for filtering on values like paths and URLs. Together, these improvements give your retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic, and semantic-search applications more complete results when you filter, so your applications return more relevant answers. S3 Vectors provides native support to store and query vectors in Amazon S3, delivering purpose-built, cost-optimized vector storage and query at billion-vector scale. With this launch, indexes in new vector buckets in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions use metadata pre-filtering by default, with no change to how you write vectors with PutVectors or run filtered queries with QueryVectors. To use pre-filtering on an existing index, update it in place with the UpdateIndexMode API. You can also compare pre-filtering against your current filtering on the same index, using a per-query parameter on QueryVectors, before you update. Metadata pre-filtering is available at no additional cost in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon S3 Vectors is available, and in the AWS China Regions. We are in the process of deploying this change and plan to complete the deployment in the coming days. To get started, use the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or the Amazon S3 console. To learn more, visit the Amazon S3 Vectors documentation and the AWS News blog .

title: Amazon SageMaker Studio simplifies getting started for new AI/ML builders with new sign-in options
text: Amazon SageMaker Studio now lets new customers sign up with their Google, GitHub, or Apple credentials and land inside a fully configured Studio environment - no traditional AWS account setup and no console navigation required. Previously, new customers who discovered a model on Hugging Face or an AWS product page had to complete a multi-step AWS account creation process, provide a credit card, navigate the AWS Console to find SageMaker AI, configure an environment, and set up IAM permissions before they could begin working. With earlier launches, we reduced environment setup to twenty seconds, pre-configured model customization permissions, and introduced deep links from Hugging Face and AWS product pages so customers could land directly inside Studio with a model pre-loaded. Now, with new sign-in options, customers complete a simplified sign-up using an existing identity, receive free credits as part of the AWS Free Tier with no credit card required in most cases, and arrive inside a ready-to-use SageMaker Studio environment where they can immediately fine-tune, evaluate, and deploy foundation models. Customers can invite team members by email, and collaborators sign in with their own email credentials to access the shared Studio environment, including shared models, notebooks, and endpoints without configuring IAM users or permissions. When a project grows beyond free credits, customers can upgrade to a paid plan and set a spend limit to stay within budget. Verified customers continue to receive default GPU access to G5, G6, G6e, and G4dn instances across endpoint deployments, training jobs, and notebooks without requesting quota increases. This feature is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where Amazon SageMaker Studio is supported. To get started, visit any supported model on Hugging Face and select "Customize and Deploy on SageMaker AI" or "Deploy on SageMaker AI," or click Get Started from the SageMaker Studio page. To learn more, see the AWS sign-up documentation and SageMaker Studio setup guide .

title: AWS Security Hub now exports findings to S3 in CSV or JSON format
text: Today, AWS Security Hub announces support for exporting findings to Amazon S3 in CSV or JSON (OCSF) format. Security teams that need findings outside the console for use cases such as compliance reporting and audit evidence can now export findings from every findings page in the Security Hub console, including Threats, Exposure, Vulnerabilities, Posture Management, Sensitive Data, and All Findings, without building and maintaining their own extraction pipelines. With this launch, you can start an export on demand from the findings page you are viewing and have Security Hub deliver the results to an S3 bucket in your account. You can choose CSV when you want to review or share findings in a spreadsheet or export in JSON if you need these findings in Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) format. Findings export is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Security Hub is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Security Hub User Guide at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-v2-findings-export.html .

title: AWS Partner Central adds Solution Matching Engine performance insights
text: AWS Partner Central now gives AWS Partners more visibility into how the Solution Matching Engine (SME) contributes to their co-sell pipeline. The Solution Matching Engine performance section in Partner Analytics helps partners understand how SME performs for their company and AWS Marketplace listings. Partners can view recommendations, SME-attributed opportunities, their share of AWS-originated opportunities, stall rate, and pipeline attributed to SME. They can filter by recommendation type or AWS Marketplace listing and explore top customer profiles by Region, industry, and segment. These insights help partners assess their visibility and decide where to improve their listings and opportunity information. All partners eligible for APN Customer Engagements (ACE) can find the section on the Opportunity pipeline analysis page under Partner Analytics in AWS Partner Central . To learn more about SME and how to strengthen your visibility with AWS sellers, read Solution Matching Engine: Your Gateway to AWS Sellers .

title: Amazon Time Sync Service adds support for microsecond-accurate time on 135 additional EC2 instance types in all commercial regions
text: Amazon Time Sync Service introduces support for microsecond-accurate time on 135 additional EC2 instance types—spanning 12 instance families—in all commercial regions. Built on Amazon's proven network infrastructure and the AWS Nitro System, microsecond-accurate time and nanosecond-precision hardware timestamps leverage the reference clocks running in the Nitro System directly, enabling customers to easily order application events, measure 1-way network latency, and increase distributed application transaction speed. The newly supported families include eight Gen8 families (C8a, C8i, C8i-flex, C8id, M8i, M8i-flex, R8a, and X8i) and four Gen9 families (C9g, C9gd, M9g, and M9gd). Starting today, customers can access microsecond-accurate time on these additional instance types by creating a Precision Time Placement Group (PTPG), a new placement strategy that allows customers to launch instances with Precision Time Protocol hardware clock (PHC) enabled. Customers that require both low network latency as well as precision time can associate a PTPG with their Cluster Placement Group (CPG), so that their low-latency workloads also benefit from microsecond-accurate time. For more information, refer to the Amazon Time Sync Service documentation .

title: AWS Transfer Family supports custom ports for public SFTP servers
text: AWS Transfer Family now lets you configure custom ports on public SFTP servers and choose a communication mode for each port. You can support clients that require different ports or start SFTP connections differently on a single server. Previously, public SFTP servers accepted connections only on port 22 and used server-first communication. With this launch, you can configure up to three ports (22, or any port from 2000 to 65535), allowing you to use the port numbers your business or network requires and offer multiple ports on one server. Some SFTP clients initiate communication themselves, and their connections can occasionally stall on a server-first port. For each port, you can now select client-first or server-first communication and direct clients to the port that matches their connection behavior. Using a port other than 22 can also reduce unwanted connection attempts from automated scanners that target port 22. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where Transfer Family public SFTP servers are offered. To get started, visit the AWS Transfer Family console or use the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit Create an SFTP-enabled server in the AWS Transfer Family User Guide

title: AWS Transform adds storage migration assessments for Amazon S3, EBS, EFS, and FSx
text: Migration assessments in AWS Transform now evaluate on-premises storage for migration to AWS. Instead of manually analyzing thousands of volumes across protocols, capacity, and performance, you upload a storage inventory and AWS Transform does the mapping for you. It matches each workload to the best-fit service, sizes the recommendation, and projects costs to produce a total cost of ownership business case. Bring NAS shares, SAN LUNs, direct-attached disks, or backup repositories via a NetApp Digital Advisor export, RVTools file, or other inventory. AWS Transform routes workloads across Amazon S3, Amazon EBS, Amazon EFS, and Amazon FSx (NetApp ONTAP, Windows File Server, OpenZFS, Lustre). Run what-if scenarios to compare deployment options such as Single-AZ vs. Multi-AZ or cost-optimized vs. performance-optimized, then ask follow-up questions about any result in chat. Storage migration assessments are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform is available. To learn more, see the AWS Transform User Guide .

title: Amazon MSK now supports configuring custom domain names for MSK Provisioned clusters
text: You can now easily configure custom domain names on Amazon MSK Provisioned clusters, on either ZooKeeper or KRaft mode for metadata management. This capability helps client applications maintain the same connection endpoints, simplifying cluster migrations, disaster recovery failovers, and scaling operations without reconfiguration. Previously, customers configured custom domain names manually on each broker. Additionally, on KRaft-based clusters, customers could not configure custom domain names. With this launch, you can now easily define a custom domain once at the cluster level, and Amazon MSK automatically applies it to every broker in the cluster, eliminating the need to configure each broker individually. The configuration persists through scaling operations and works identically on both ZooKeeper and KRaft-based clusters. This is particularly useful for customers who route traffic through Network Load Balancers, require persistent endpoints across cluster operations, or must adhere to organizational naming conventions for security and compliance. You can configure custom domain names on all new and existing MSK Provisioned clusters, in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Provisioned is available, at no additional cost. To learn more, see the Amazon MSK Developer Guide .

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports Graviton4 based i8ge instances
text: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports i8ge instances, which is the latest generation of storage optimized instances offering the best performance for storage-intensive workloads. Powered by AWS Graviton4 processors, I8ge instances deliver up to 60% better compute performance compared to previous generation Graviton2-based storage optimized Im4gn instances. I8ge instances use the latest third generation AWS Nitro SSDs, local NVMe storage that deliver up to 55% better real-time storage performance per TB while offering up to 60% lower storage I/O latency and up to 75% lower storage I/O latency variability compared to previous generation Im4gn instances. Built on the AWS Nitro System , these instances oﬄoad CPU virtualization, storage, and networking functions to dedicated hardware and software enhancing the performance and security for your workloads. I8ge instances are available of sizes up to 18xlarge and 45 TB instance storage. At 112.5 Gbps, these instances have the highest networking bandwidth among storage optimized instances available in Amazon OpenSearch Service. I8ge instances support all OpenSearch versions & Elasticsearch (open source) versions 7.9 and 7.10. Amazon OpenSearch Service supports i8ge instances in following AWS Regions : US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Singapore) and Asia Pacific (Sydney). For region specific availability & pricing, visit our pricing page . To learn more about Amazon OpenSearch Service and its capabilities, visit our product page .

title: AWS AppConfig launches managed experimentation tools for A/B testing
text: Today, AWS announces the general availability of experimentation tools in AWS AppConfig, a new capability that enables you to run A/B tests and feature experiments without building or managing separate experimentation infrastructure. Built on 25+ years of Amazon experimentation best practices, AWS AppConfig experimentation tools use AI-driven guidance to help you build robust experiments while providing exposure control and locked treatment allocations so you can make confident, data-driven decisions about what to ship to your customers. Using AWS AppConfig experimentation tools, you can run A/B tests and multivariate experiments across your application stack, from UI changes and recommendation algorithms to AI model selections and prompt experiments. Define feature variations, target granular audiences using a rule builder, and set traffic allocation percentages through the AWS Management Console, CLI, API, or AWS CDK. AI-assisted experiment design can validate your setup against Amazon's best practices, helping you build experiments with sufficient statistical power. Customers set up and run the experiment in AWS AppConfig, and then analyze results using Amazon CloudWatch or existing analytics tools. At the end of the experiment, you promote the winning treatment to production through a standard AWS AppConfig safe rollout. Experiments work across workloads on Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, and on-premises servers through AWS AppConfig Agent.

title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports disaggregated prefill and decode
text: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports Disaggregated Prefill and Decode (DPD), an inference optimization that separates the two phases of large language model (LLM) inference — prefill and decode — onto dedicated GPU pools and transfers the key-value (KV) cache between them over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) using GPU-Direct RDMA. Customers running LLMs in production for chat assistants, agentic pipelines, retrieval-augmented generation, and long-document analysis need consistent per-token latency and predictable throughput under mixed traffic, but when prefill and decode share the same GPU, a single long-context request can stall token generation for every concurrent request and force customers to over-provision one phase to protect the other. With DPD, customers run compute-bound prefill on one set of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound decode on another, so the two phases no longer contend for the same resources. This delivers more consistent per-token latency under sustained concurrency, higher goodput at strict latency SLOs, and the ability to scale prefill and decode capacity independently to match the input and output distribution of the workload. An intelligent router automatically directs long-context requests through the disaggregated path and sends shorter prompts directly to the decoder, so customers get the benefit on the traffic that needs it without paying transfer overhead on short prompts. Customers enable DPD by adding a `pdSpec` section to the same `InferenceEndpointConfig` custom resource they already use for inference endpoints on the HyperPod Inference Operator, and DPD is composable with the existing KV cache offloading and intelligent routing features on HyperPod. DPD is available for SageMaker HyperPod clusters using the EKS orchestrator on EFA-capable instance types in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker HyperPod is available. To learn more, see Disaggregated Prefill and Decode for HyperPod inference in the Amazon SageMaker AI Developer Guide.

title: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) clusters now support up to 256 TiB of storage volume
text: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) now supports a maximum storage limit of 256 TiB, doubling the previous limit of 128 TiB. This enhancement allows customers to store and manage even larger datasets within a single DocumentDB cluster, simplifying data management for large-scale applications and supporting the growing data needs of modern applications. Customers only pay for the storage they use, with no need for upfront provisioning of the full 256 TiB. To access the increased storage limit, upgrade your cluster to supported engine versions. Once upgraded, DocumentDB storage will automatically scale up to 256 TiB capacity based on the amount of data in the cluster volume. Visit technical documentation to learn more about supported versions. This new storage volume capacity is available in all AWS regions where Amazon DocumentDB is available. Amazon DocumentDB is a serverless, fully managed, MongoDB API-compatible document database service. It provides built-in security, continuous backups, up to 15 read replicas, Global Clusters for automated multi-Region replication, and integrations with other AWS services. To get started with Amazon DocumentDB, take a look at our getting started page .

title: AWS PrivateLink announces Tunnel Endpoints to access network segments
text: AWS PrivateLink customers can now use VPC endpoint to privately and securely access network segments in another VPC/account. They can use a ‘tunnel’ endpoint, a new type of VPC endpoint, to tunnel into the network segment and access resources located within it. AWS PrivateLink is a highly available and scalable technology that enables private access across VPC and account boundaries to load balanced services, appliances, and resources such as databases and domains. Prior to this launch, customers who wanted to share their resources with another party such as an external vendor had to do it one at a time by creating a Resource Configuration for every resource. Now, customers can create a Resource Configuration to represent a CIDR range in their network, and share it with a vendor via AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM). The vendor can then create a tunnel endpoint and use GENEVE encapsulation to tunnel through it into the customer’s VPC to access resources located in CIDR range specified by the customer. There is an hourly charge for the tunnel endpoint and a per-GB charge for data processed through it. Please refer to the pricing page for AWS PrivateLink . The capability is available in the following AWS Regions : US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Canada West (Calgary), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Milan), Europe (Paris), Europe (Spain), Europe (Stockholm), Europe (Zurich), Mexico (Central), South America (São Paulo). To learn more about this capability and get started, please refer to the AWS PrivateLink documentation .
